recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-16984 unless a future worker separately audits the later FHIR-38824 clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-16984 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core STU3 datatype issue asking to clarify ContactPoint.rank so it did not imply the order of repeated ContactPoint elements. The requested wording says ContactPoints with lower rank values are more preferred than those with higher rank values.
initial_application: Jira records svn revision 14299. In the git mirror, e8f0a1acb64f4c98a41dc4ebd4899d9665efc1c0 is that git-svn revision and directly replaced the old 'Contacts are ranked with lower values coming before higher values' sentence with the requested ContactPoints/lower-rank wording in source/datatypes/contactpoint.xml.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists ContactPoint as an active datatype and marks it normative, putting source/datatypes/contactpoint.xml in current build scope. Later Published issue FHIR-38824 added examples for equal, absent, and non-sequential ContactPoint.rank values; that later clarification complements FHIR-16984 and explains the broader current comment text.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current ContactPoint.rank row already contains the FHIR-16984 clarification and the surrounding comment states that rank does not necessarily follow the order in which contacts appear in an instance.

related_jiras.note: Published R5 clarification for the same ContactPoint.rank row added examples for duplicate, absent, and non-sequential ranks, supporting that the current broader comments are intentional and not a conflict with FHIR-16984.
